newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas soars to $3/GJ at Alberta hub.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas soars to $3/GJ at Alberta hub.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were up sharply in Alberta on Monday, as severely cold temperatures struck western Canada, draining supplies.
At the AECO storage hub, next-day prices gained about 70 cents to reach the C$3.00 per gigajoule (GJ) level, as the thermometer in Calgary read about -34 degrees Celsius (-29 Fahrenheit).

"Most people are focusing on short-term stuff. This cold is supposed to last at least for another week," one Calgary-based trader said, noting storage withdrawals at the hub were at their maximum rate.
January prices were quoted at C$2.29 and C$2.30, up about 20 cents from December indices.
Most traders said they expected these prices to move higher due to the sharp upward movement in the daily market.

At Sumas, Wash., the Canada/U.S. border, forecasts for milder temperatures in the Northwest and an anticipated drop in demand over the holiday pushed prices into the $3.90-4.00 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range early, down more than 20 cents from Friday.
Late deals were heard done as low as $3.85.
At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, prices for Tuesday delivery fell by about 40 cents to the $4.10-4.15 per mmBtu level.
"It's quiet. There's not much getting done," one source said, adding that mild temperatures in the East and the upcoming holiday were the two major factors putting downward pressure on the market.
Temperatures in the East are expected to drop later this week, but the lack of market participants may be enough to counteract the increase in heating demand, sources said.
